mainEntity.name: How old is my dog in human years?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on age and size. A medium dog aged 5 is about 36 human years by the veterinary table, and the epigenetic formula gives a higher figure for the same age. Enter your dog's details above.

mainEntity.name: Why do large dogs age faster?

acceptedAnswer.text: Larger breeds grow quickly and tend to have shorter lifespans, so each later calendar year represents more biological aging than for a small dog. Giant breeds often reach senior status by 6 to 7 years.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate a cat's age in human years?

acceptedAnswer.text: The common guideline counts the first year as 15, the second year as 24, and then adds 4 for each year after that. A 10-year-old cat is about 56 human years.

mainEntity.name: What is the epigenetic clock formula?

acceptedAnswer.text: Researchers at the University of California San Diego compared DNA methylation in dogs and humans and found human age ≈ 16 × ln(dog age) + 31. It was developed from Labrador retrievers, so it may not fit every breed.

mainEntity.name: When is a pet a senior?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cats are considered mature at 7 to 10 years and senior from about 11. Dogs become senior earlier the larger they are, from roughly 6 to 7 for giant breeds to 10 or more for small dogs.
